en: The Ritual Manual for Attaining Buddhahood through the Contemplation of the Body, the Secret Yoga of the Equality of Mañjuśrī.
Translated by the State Preceptor of the Great Qidan Kingdom of the Song Dynasty, [from] Central India.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Cixian of the Kingdom of Magadha. Whenever one wishes to perform recitations, ritual services, or offerings, one should first take refuge in the Buddha and contemplate the Eight Great Vows.
The mantra is as follows:
Upon first entering the maṇḍala, face toward the Buddha.
Sit and contemplate this body as being shattered like fine dust. Then, withdraw and gather the body back together.
The mantra for the vajra-body is as follows:
Oṃ rājopagata sarvadharmāḥ svāhā. (The purification of the four karmas of speech.
Oṃ vajratāḍana sarvatramān vajratāḍaya hūṃ. (The purification of the three karmas of mind.)
Oṃ kīta dhā sarva rāma kīta dha haṃ. The three karmas of body, speech, and mind are purified.

Once the three karmas are purified, one directs the mind toward all sentient beings within the six realms of existence, [to purify] their retributive obstacles, karmic obstacles, afflictive obstacles, and so forth.
All [impurities] are completely extinguished and one attains purity.
Next, visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala above and mentally perform offerings.
Furthermore, imagine that your own hands become Vajrapāṇi.
The feet, eyes, heart, and so forth are likewise treated in this manner.
Having performed prostrations and services to the Buddhas with one’s adamantine body,
one should then further visualize the five fingers of one's own hands.
Taking the five nectars of Vajrajñāna, one sprinkles them upon one’s own crown.
One washes away the five bodies, the ten karmas, and the six sense-objects,
visualizing that the ordinary body is entirely non-existent.
Upon a pure lunar disc, one visualizes one’s own body in the form of the syllable HŪṂ, like a flame of light,
resting upon the moon disc with the size of a lamp. One should recite this mantra seven times while maintaining this visualization.
The mantra is:
Oṃ jñānamudrānaya me. Furthermore, one should visualize the form of the syllable Hūṃ, which abides upon the lunar disc.
Like a great mass of light,
one visualizes the sparks of fire from the body dispersing;
after a short while, they are gathered back again.
Recite the mantra seven times.
Furthermore, visualize a small radiance upon the lunar disc, abide therein while reciting this mantra; it should be done seven times.
The mantra is as follows:
*Kṣi-prabha-acala*. Visualize the body spinning and departing again, while reciting this mantra;
it should also be performed seventeen times.
The mantra is as follows:
Visualize the body coming forth again; recite the mantra seven times.
The mantra is: [Mantra].
Furthermore, visualize entering the body; as you are about to achieve the body of Great Enlightenment, recite this secret mantra, empowering it seventeen times.
The mantra is as follows:
Visualize a small radiance abiding [within], like the body of the Great Awakened One;
while reciting this dhāraṇī, one should further chant the mantra seven times.
Furthermore, one should contemplate one's own body as being of vajra-nature, just like the body of a Tathāgata, identical and without distinction.
Recite this mantra three times: Oṃ yathā sarvatathāgatasatyaṃ hūṃ. Next, one should hold a vajra in the right hand.
The left hand holds a bell, performing the pāramitā mudrā.
The bodhisattva holds a ritual vajra (kē-chǔ) to represent the Buddha-seal;
its five prongs symbolize the Tathāgata.
The bell symbolizes the four pāramitās.
The bodhisattva clearly visualizes himself as Ratnasambhava Buddha and hurls the vajra three times.
Next, one should perform the circular dance and form the lotus mudrā.
Having formed the mudrā, prostrate;
having prostrated, grasp the vajra.
At the tips of the fingers, the mouth,
and the heart, recite Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ—
the three syllables of wisdom.
Visualize the crown as a maṇḍala.
First, visualize a lotus flower placed within the crown;
that lotus has eight petals.
Having settled the lotus,
one next lies upon the vajra;
atop that vajra are the discs of the sun and moon.
Upon the solar disc are twelve syllables;
upon the lunar disc are further sixteen—
the mothers of the Brahmī script.
Since the phenomenon of birth cannot be apprehended,
one should visualize the syllable Oṃ resting upon a lunar disc.
Furthermore, one contemplates the syllable Oṃ as it revolves and departs;
after a long while, it returns and forms the shape of a wheel.
One then visualizes this once more as Vairocana Buddha.
The Buddhas of the other four directions are arranged in sequence,
all equal to the four pāramitās; they dwell in the four corners,
contemplating the knowledge of all modes, seated upon three-tiered thrones.
There is no lunar disc.
This applies down to the vidyārāja;
all should be treated in this manner.
The aforementioned nine figures reside in the first court;
the eight inner bodhisattvas contemplate the syllables of the seed-wisdom (*jñāna-bīja*),
which are distributed sequentially throughout the second court.
The twelve outer deities, the ten Vidyārājas, and so forth,
likewise recollecting their seed-syllables and secret names,
are established in their respective positions within the third enclosure.
When the visualization of the maṇḍala is complete,
one contemplates one's own body as being the Buddha,
and then immediately recollects the Buddha-maṇḍala.
The mantra is as follows:

*Buddhavajradharaśrīmantra-tirvavajra-binyāpavinā-adhiṣṭhānapraṇaminiyaṃ-kāruṇyakavajriṇa-naśanaiḥsaṃstuta-buddha-krīḍāmbho-kāyavajriṇa-oṃ sarvatathāgata-kāyavajra-svāhā svātmako haṃ*. Then, one should visualize the arrangement of the Dharma-maṇḍala within the mouth.
Visualize the syllable *A*.
As it departs and returns, it becomes a precious lotus flower.
Again, visualize it once more as Amitābha.
Visualize as before.
One should recollect the Dharma-maṇḍala.
The mantra is as follows:

Dharmavegavāhasiri-mantra-tirvavajra-bhinyapavinā-adhiṣṭhānapraṇamini-yaṃ kāruṇyavāgvajrāna naśanaiḥ saṃskṛta-mahā-kuccha-vantu vāgvajrāna oṃ sarva tathāgata vajrasvabhāva-ātma-koṭi. Then, one should visualize the Saṅgha mandala within the heart.
Visualize the form of the syllable HŪṂ.
Departing and returning again constitutes the Vajra;
contemplate that in a single turn, one becomes the Honored One Akṣobhya.
Performing the same visualization as before,
one should then bring to mind the Sangha altar.
The dhāraṇī is as follows:
Having visualized the Three Jewels, settle the mind in tranquil immobility;
then, with the vajra-noose, bind and close the gates of the six sense faculties.
Binding each one in succession as it arises, one is as if clad in adamantine armor.
The mantra is:
Oṃ chindhi hūṃ vajra-kīla. Next, one should with a sincere heart take refuge in the Three Jewels and the maṇḍala.
Then recite the dhāraṇī.
Having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, visualize before you a single altar,
beneath which are the elements of wind, fire, and water, with the earth mandala situated at the very top.
Upon the earth, four-colored iron; upon the iron, triangular earth—this constitutes the ground of variegated jewels.
Next, join the palms of both hands at the heart and place them upon the ground.
For the Vajra [rite], no mandala is required.
Having thus established [the seat], one should visualize the syllable Ā residing within the maṇḍala;
imagine that the syllable departs and returns, resting upon a precious lotus flower.
Next, one should visualize the syllable HŪṂ.
Abiding as the Jewel-Vajra, one further visualizes the syllable *Bhrūṃ Oṃ* as a pavilion of the seven precious gems;
within it is a three-tiered altar with four gates, each gate being of a different color.
Visualize white in the east, blue in the south, yellow in the west,
and golden in the north; within that pavilion, visualize the disks of the sun and moon,
and further recite Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ, visualizing them upon the lunar disk.
Furthermore, visualize the body of the syllable Oṃ transforming into the form of a Buddha-wheel;
then one should further imagine the syllable A becoming a precious lotus flower;
and again visualize the essence of the syllable Hūṃ forming the Wisdom-Vajra.
Thereafter, one visualizes the three syllables;
they depart together and return again to abide within the mandala— the five Buddhas, the pāramitās,
the twelve inner and outer deities, the ten Great Vidyārājas, and so forth.
The types of knowledge and their sequence are as extensively explained above.
Next, form the lotus mudrā with both hands and visualize receiving the Tathāgata from above.
Recite this mantra three times.
Visualize that the Buddhas of the upper direction have been invited and have descended into the mandala;
while reciting this mantra, direct your mind toward the eastern gate and pay homage.
Visualizing that the Buddha has arrived at the altar, one seeks the empowerment of the precious vase and recites this mantra.
Directing the mind toward the southern gate, one performs prostrations;
then, visualizing that the empowerment has been conferred, one takes refuge in the Tathāgata.
Practicing according to the Dharma, one should extensively present the Dharma-offering and recite this mantra.
Visualizing oneself at the western gate,
one should then visualize one's own body as firm, unarisen, and undying.
In performing these deeds there is no end; one should make offerings to the Buddha.
May all sentient beings obtain the fruit of *siddhi*.
Reciting this mantra, one should imagine bowing at the northern gate.
Again, he earnestly addressed the Buddha: "I shall now, with sincere devotion, offer worship according to my means;
taking refuge in the Tathāgata, I shall recite this gāthā and pay homage at the eastern gate toward the center."

Next, praise with the five Buddhas and sing hymns to the Tathāgata. Prostrate to the four Buddhas in the four directions: In the east, prostrate to the Honored One named Jñānavajrakāya (Wisdom-Vajra-Body).

*Oṃ kṛ-vi-jra vajra mahānirjara vajradhātu mahābuddha tīrmaṇḍala tīrvajragara kuśavajra namo stute Vairocana-tathāgata-buddhavajrakāya.* In the south, prostrate to the Honored One named Ratnavajrakāya (Jewel-Vajra-Body). *Oṃ kṛ-vi-jra vajra mahānirjara vajradhātu mahābuddha tīrmaṇḍala tīrvajragara kuśavajra namo stute Ratnasambhava-tathāgata-ratnavajrakāya.* In the west, prostrate to the Honored One named Dharmavajrakāya (Dharma-Vajra-Body). *Oṃ kṛ-vi-jra vajra mahānirjara vajradhātu mahābuddha tīrmaṇḍala tīrvajragara kuśavajra namo stute Amitābha-tathāgata-dharmavajrakāya.* In the north, prostrate to the Honored One named Karmavajrakāya (Action-Vajra-Body). *Oṃ kṛ-vi-jra vajra mahānirjara vajradhātu mahābuddha tīrmaṇḍala tīrvajragara kuśavajra namo stute Amoghasiddhi-tathāgata-karmavajrakāya.* Finally, prostrate to the Honored One in the center named Jñānavajrakāya. *Oṃ kṛ-vi-jra vajra mahānirjara vajradhātu mahābuddha tīrmaṇḍala tīrvajragara kuśavajra namo stute Vairocana-tathāgata-buddhavajrakāya.*
Vairocana (1), Mahāvajra (2), Vajrasattva (3), Mahārati (4), Prākṛti (5), Prasavāragraha (6), Niveśa-vajra (7). Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava, whose body is the Jewel-Vajra (8).
Ratnarāja (1) Suyanbhira-kha (2) Vajrakāśa (3) Nirmala (4) Svabhāvadha (5) Nṛpe (6) Kāya-vajra (7) Namaḥ-stute (8). Amitābha Tathāgata, the Vajra-Amitābha, the Body of Immortal Nectar.
Vajramūrti, Mahānijana, Nṛvīkara, Vajradarika, Rāgapramardi, Prabhāta, Vāsava-vajra, Namo-stute. O Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, Vajrabodhisattva-body.
Having chanted praises to the five buddhas,
visualize the earth-maṇḍala arising and placing it upon the crown of your head; like wearing a diadem,
the two maṇḍalas merge into one, as water and milk blend together, and you sit therein.
Each, without making distinctions, sits calmly and reflects with discernment;
forming the mudrā while recollecting the fundamental mantra, they occupy their respective positions as honored deities.
The mudrā of Tathāgata Akṣobhya is formed by placing the left fist at the navel.
For Vairocana Buddha: the right hand forms the vajra-fist mudrā of Ratnasambhava Tathāgata; the left fist is placed at the navel.
For Amitābha Tathāgata: both hands are turned upward and interlaced.
The fingers of the *vīrya* (effort) mudrā are held upright with their backs against each other; at their tips, the *dhyāna* (meditation) and *prajñā* (wisdom) fingers are placed crosswise.
This is the mudrā of Akṣobhya-Vajrasattva. For the Vajrapāramitā, one forms the left fist and places it at the navel;
both hands then form the Vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*).

The Seal of the Jewel Pāramitā: without altering the previous seal, for the Seal of the Dharma Pāramitā, open the two hands in the *vajra-pañjali* gesture, with the *kṣānti*, *praṇidhi*, *vīrya*, and *bala* fingers;
place them upon the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* [fingers] as described above.
The Karmapāramitā [Mudrā]: Regarding the mudrās corresponding to the twenty deities of the Vajrabandha Bodhisattva, they shall now be explained.
With both hands in the Vajrabandha [mudrā], pull them apart to the left and right.
The Mudrā of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva: Form the Vajrabandha with both hands in a whirling dance gesture;
With palms facing upward, open and spread them downward to the positions of the various deities; First bind, then whirl in dance.
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva: The left fist rests at the side of the waist;
the right hand is in the *varada-mudrā*. The *dhyāna* finger presses upon the *kṣānti* finger.
This is the secret mudrā of Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva: the left fist is again placed at the waist.
The right hand is at the heart; with the *dhyāna-mudrā*, press the ring finger (*anāmikā*) and middle finger (*madhyamā*).
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has his left fist placed at the side of the waist, the right fingers bent at the *śīla* finger (*tarjanī*), turning clockwise and resting at the heart in a relaxed manner.

The Seal of Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin: With both hands in the *vajra-vīrya* (advancing power) hook-sattva mudrā, place the left fist at the waist and the right hand at the side of the navel;
bend the ring finger and middle finger (*dhyāna*) and pinch the forefinger (*vīrya*).
The mudrā of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva: the left fist is placed at the waist;
with the right hand, the fingers are held in the *dhyāna-muṣṭi* (meditation-fist) at the level of the ribs. The two eyes follow the movement of the hand.
The mudrā of Maitreya Bodhisattva: the left fist is placed at the side of the waist.
The right hand is at the front of the heart; form the *kṣānti-mudrā* (the "patience" gesture) with the middle fingers interlaced to offer clothing to the Bodhisattva.
The left fist rests at the waist while the right hand faces forward; snap the *kṣānti* finger and release.
The Mudrā of the Bodhisattva Guanhua: With the right hand, hold it within the left palm as if grasping a flower.
Visualize it placed upon the Buddha’s crown. The Seal of the Bodhisattva Sankhua:
With the left hand, form the *jñāna-muṣṭi* (wisdom-fist) and press the *praṇidhi* (vow) finger.
The right hand forms the *dhyāna-muṣṭi* (meditation fist) with the fingers pointing outward;
this is the mudrā of the Bodhisattva who Scatters Incense before one. The two hands hold an incense burner;
this is the mudrā of the Bodhisattva who Makes Offerings of Lamps. The left hand cradles the right hand.
The Mudrā of the Bodhisattva Amṛta: Visualize that within the palm of the left hand there is the water of nectar (*amṛta*);
with the index finger of the right hand, snap the fingers as an offering to the Bodhisattva; place the left fist at the waist.
The right hand is held before the face in the manner of grasping a mirror;
with both hands making a dancing gesture, one performs the offering of song to the Bodhisattva,
while the left fist rests at the side of the waist.
Right hand, with fingers extended and pointing forward, held upright and clapped together:
Oṃ vajragīte hūṃ. At this point, one should employ the mantras and mudrās of the ten Great Vidyārājas.
As detailed extensively in another fascicle,
having performed the secret offerings, one further presents food and drink,
flowers, fruits, and unguents, making offerings of various kinds.
If the mind becomes weary and one cannot complete all the ritual procedures,
and wishes to depart from the maṇḍala, one should recollect the offering of light and then reflect with clear mindfulness,
looking up to address all the Tathāgatas:
I offer this mental visualization with devotion;
should there be any errors, may the Buddha compassionately regard me.
May he again bestow the nectar of his Dharma to wash away all my transgressions, so that they may all be utterly extinguished.
The Vajrācārya bestows the initiation upon the disciple as described above.
First, one should visualize the maṇḍala; furthermore, one should recite the secret mantra, namely the four Vidyārājas:
the *praṇidhāna* (or *praṇaya*) *taka* mantra, using which one should snap flowers to strike away the five obstacles (*pañcāvaraṇa*) of the disciple with the *pātana* Vidyārāja mantra.
Then, one should burn white mustard seeds and fumigate the recipient of the dharma;
all afflictions [are thereby removed]. King Ṭakkirāja empowers pure water, which is then sprinkled upon the body of the disciple.
Thus one removes all stains of sin;
by using the *pradīpa* mantra to consecrate cooked rice, one makes offerings to the devas, nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of beings. This rite is most secret.
One must not propagate this recklessly; it may only be proclaimed to those who have met with wise people.
This is the ritual procedure for attaining Buddhahood by contemplating the body, the Secret Yoga of the Equality of Mañjuśrī.
